summary: Peter Alan Roberts works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed doctoral studies supervised by Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

Peter C. Bisschop is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2004 under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at Edinburgh (2005–2010), Leiden (2010), and Oxford.

Peter Connolly is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Lancaster University and became a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and under traditional teachers Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim and Seungsahn Haengwon. He served at the East-West Center.
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and advisers N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, and held a post at Deakin University.

Peter Francis Kornicki works in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oxford (DLitt 2011) and Tokyo, he held posts at the University of Tasmania (1978–1982), Kyoto University (~1982–1985), and the University of Cambridge (~1985).

Peter Friedlander is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (1983–1991) and was an associate professor at the Australian National University in 2013.

Peter Gaeffke was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at Mainz (1948–1952) and studied at Regensburg and DIAS. He served as professor at Utrecht University (1965–1975) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).
Peter Gerlitz was a religious studies scholar who studied under Friedrich Heiler and held a post at the University of Bremen.

Peter Giles was a linguist who studied at Aberdeen, Cambridge, Freiburg, and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and John Peile. He served at Emmanuel College from 1887 and became Reader in Comparative Philology at Cambridge in 1891.
Peter Gyallay-Pap is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the London School of Economics by 1990 and was an adjunct at Adams State University (attested 2007).

Peter Hartmann was a linguist, Indologist, and Japanologist who earned his PhD at Münster under Alfred Schmitt. He served as professor of linguistics at the University of Münster (from 1956) and the University of Konstanz (1969).

Peter Harvey is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (1976–2011) and founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996.
Peter Haskel works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson earned his PhD at Yale (~1956–1961). He taught at Yale (~1961–1964), Vassar College, the University of Washington (~1964–1970), Bennington College (~1970–1971), and the University of Otago (~1971–1999).

Peter James Gilks specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, earned a PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers, and studied under several Geshes and Khensurs.

Peter K. Austin is a linguist who earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He served as Foundation Professor at the University of Melbourne (1996–2002) and Emeritus Professor at SOAS University of London (2002–2018).
Peter Koret is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kuhlmann is a linguist who completed his doctorate under Rosemarie Lühr (~1990–1993). He held posts at the University of Düsseldorf (~2001–2002), the University of Giessen (~2002–2004), and the University of Göttingen (~2004).
